solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Rising temperature, fan reversed

indicators.note: something reversed runs the other way

parts.note: T is the standard abbreviation for temperature
a fan of something is a lover of it

explanation.surface: A heat gauge climbs while an electric fan spins the wrong way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rising' reads as the temperature going up, but it is a noun here, as in the Easter Rising. The reversal covers both pieces, so TLOVER turns round whole.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a rising is an uprising, a rebellion against authority.

clue.text: On the verge of verbal attack, the leader's left

indicators.note: the leader, the first letter, has left the building, so drop B from the front

parts.note: a fierce verbal attack, named after a warship firing all the guns on one side

explanation.surface: Someone is about to launch into a tirade just as the boss walks out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the verge of' looks like 'about to', but the verge is the grass strip beside a road; 'of' only joins the halves.
explanation.definitionFit: British usage: the verge is the grassy strip along a road, so anything on it sits beside the road.

clue.text: One with bedside material about heroism

indicators.note: one thing placed about another surrounds it, so the bed material wraps round the one

parts.note: the fabric skirt hanging round the side of a bed
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone sits by a hospital bed with a book about heroism.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Material' looks like subject matter for reading, but it is fabric; the answer is a rarer form of valour.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the state of being valiant is courage, heroism.

clue.text: Sleep on vehicle regularly returning home

indicators.note: at regular intervals, so take every other letter of vehicle
something returning comes back, so those letters run the other way

parts.note: the even letters of vEhIcLe are EIL, turned round
to be home is to be in

explanation.surface: Someone dozes on the bus as it makes its regular run home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sleep on' is the verb phrase: to go on sleeping instead of getting up.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: to stay in bed past the usual hour is to go on sleeping.

clue.text: Tenants dressed like monks

parts.note: dressed in something
a monk's robe is a habit

explanation.surface: Residents who go about in robes like a religious order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tenants' looks like a plural noun, but it is the verb: one tenants a house by living in it.
explanation.definitionFit: A verb sense: to tenant a place is to occupy and live in it.

clue.text: It's a sum arranged with mints who deal in coins

definitions.note: a relative clause standing for the people themselves

indicators.note: letters that are arranged are set out in a new order

parts.note: anagram fodder, 7 letters
anagram fodder, 5 letters, added by 'with'

explanation.surface: Coin traders tot up their money with the mints that strike it.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is all money, so 'mints' and 'sum' look like part of the definition; they are letters only.
explanation.definitionFit: Coin collectors and dealers are the people who study and trade coins.

clue.text: Taking office in so scenic a complex

indicators.note: something complex is tangled, so the letters are knotted into a new arrangement

parts.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters

explanation.surface: A new official moves into an office block with splendid views.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Complex' looks like a building, fitting the office picture, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: coming to a throne or high office, as a monarch does.

clue.text: Being retired around mid-forty is natural

indicators.note: the middle of a word, so take the central letter of forty

parts.note: someone who has retired for the night is in bed

indicators.note: one thing around another encloses it, so IN BED goes round the letter

parts.note: R is the middle letter of foRty

explanation.surface: Someone who stops work in their mid-forties finds it comes naturally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retired' suggests leaving work, but here it means gone to bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an inborn quality is natural rather than learned.

clue.text: Music player over before empty tapes turned up

indicators.note: an empty word has lost its contents, leaving only the outside letters of tapes
in a down clue, something turned up is flipped to read upwards

parts.note: O is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for an over
an old word for before
TapeS with its inside removed

explanation.surface: The player stopped before the cassettes, now blank, were flipped.
explanation.walkthrough: OERETS read upwards gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a hi-fi system for playing records and tapes.

clue.text: Mass meetings not run to make friends

indicators.note: not run means without run, so the R is left out

parts.note: a rally is a mass meeting
remove R, the cricket abbreviation for a run

explanation.surface: Big gatherings where nobody runs off, so people bond.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mass meetings' looks like the definition, but it is the wordplay; the definition sits at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: those on your side in a dispute are your friends.

clue.text: A taxi stopping spilt lime cordial

indicators.note: something spilt is scattered, so LIME's letters land in a new order

parts.note: used as it stands

indicators.note: a stopper plugs a gap, so the taxi sits inside the mixed-up lime

parts.note: LIME rearranged
a taxi

explanation.surface: A cab pulls up beside a spilled bottle of lime cordial.
explanation.walkthrough: A + MI(CAB)LE. Lime cordial is a fruit drink in the surface; the definition is the adjective cordial, meaning friendly.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a cordial greeting is warm and friendly.

clue.text: Man and son, in love with girl, act Platonically

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it

parts.note: a man's name
love is zero in tennis, O
a girl's name
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A father and son, both keen on a girl, keep things purely platonic.
explanation.walkthrough: PHIL + O + SOPHI(S)E. 'Platonically' suggests chaste, non-romantic love, which fits the girl; the capital P points to Plato himself.
explanation.definitionFit: Plato is the archetypal thinker, so to behave in his manner is to reason about ideas.

clue.text: Stays in reliable establishments on vacation

parts.note: a reliable supporter is a staunch one

indicators.note: a place on vacation is vacated, emptied, so only its outside letters remain

parts.note: EstablishmentS emptied of its middle

explanation.surface: Someone stays at trusty hotels while on holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stays' looks like lodging at a hotel; here it is the verb to stay, meaning to stop or check a flow.
explanation.definitionFit: A verb sense: to stay bleeding is to stop its flow.

clue.text: Material influenced by a vocalist

indicators.note: a vocalist uses the voice, so the word is to be heard rather than read

parts.note: influenced means moved or persuaded; say that word and you hear a fabric

explanation.surface: A fabric choice was swayed by a singer's taste.
explanation.walkthrough: SWAYED, spoken, sounds like SUEDE. 'Vocalist' makes it sound musical, but it only signals speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: napped leather used for shoes and jackets.

clue.text: With many stresses last month, basically shattered

indicators.note: something shattered is broken into pieces, so basically is broken up and rebuilt

parts.note: the calendar abbreviation for December, the last month of the year
anagram fodder, 9 letters

explanation.surface: Someone under heavy strain last month is now completely exhausted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stresses' looks like worries; it means stressed syllables. A ten-syllable line, such as iambic pentameter, carries five stresses.
explanation.definitionFit: A poetic sense: a ten-syllable line carries several stressed beats.

clue.text: English poet martyred expertly by a Pole

parts.note: one of the Earth's two poles
done expertly is done well

explanation.surface: An English poet is skilfully put to death by a Polish man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' reads as a Polish person, but it is a geographic pole. Robert Southwell was a Jesuit poet executed under Elizabeth I in 1595.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Robert Southwell, author of 'The Burning Babe', was hanged at Tyburn and later canonised.

clue.text: Two notes, one that's not true or friendly

parts.note: two notes of the do-re-mi scale
one who does not tell the truth

explanation.surface: Two short messages, one of them false or at least overfriendly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Or' only joins the wordplay to the definition here.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: informal and friendly, sometimes too much so.

clue.text: Glance at one interrupting exercise in a mean way

parts.note: to glance quickly over a text

indicators.note: someone interrupting breaks into the middle, so I goes inside the word for exercise

parts.note: to ply a skill or trade is to exercise it
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone peers over at a person meanly cutting into their workout.
explanation.walkthrough: SKIM + P(I)LY. 'Exercise' wants to be PE, but it is the verb ply.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: done meanly is done with too little, stingily.

clue.text: Quiz score?

parts.note: the surface wants a pub quiz; the setter means a query, a single question
the surface wants points won; the setter means a line scored on a page, a written sign

explanation.surface: Asking what someone got in the pub quiz.
explanation.walkthrough: It reads as points on a quiz; take quiz as 'question' and score as 'mark', a line scratched on a page, and you get the punctuation sign that ends a question.
explanation.definitionFit: Read quiz as a query and score as a written line, and the phrase describes the sign that ends every query.

clue.text: Plan to raise a baby

indicators.note: to raise something is to lift it, and in a down clue that makes the word read upwards

parts.note: a map is a plan of an area
a means each, as in 'ten pounds a head'

explanation.surface: Parents make a plan for bringing up their newborn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raise a baby' is the upbringing, but 'baby' is a verb meaning to coddle.
explanation.definitionFit: A verb sense: to baby someone is to coddle and indulge them.

clue.text: Seaside resort overlooking the Isle of Dogs

indicators.note: to overlook something is to ignore it, so the isle's letter is left out

parts.note: canines are dogs
I is the map abbreviation for island or isle, taken out

explanation.surface: A beach town with a view of the Isle of Dogs, a district of East London.
explanation.walkthrough: The Isle of Dogs is a place in London's Docklands, so the phrase looks like one name; split it and take the isle out of the dogs.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a resort on the French Riviera, home of the film festival.

clue.text: Leave embarrassed from a party

parts.note: used as it stands
an informal word for a party, as in a birthday do

explanation.surface: Someone walks out of a party red-faced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leave' looks like going away; here it means to cause, to leave someone embarrassed.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to put someone out of countenance, leaving them red-faced.

clue.text: Metal vessel with a small problem carrying current

indicators.note: something carrying a load holds it, so the problem's letters hold the current inside them

parts.note: a pot is a vessel
used as it stands
S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small
an arithmetic problem
I is the physics symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A metal pot with a small fault is conducting electricity.
explanation.walkthrough: POT + A + S + S(I)UM.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: one of the soft alkali metals, symbol K.

clue.text: Arrest a number of Parisians

definitions.meaning: to arrest a suspect is to take hold of them
a number in French, the language of Paris: sixteen

explanation.surface: Police detain a group of people from Paris.
explanation.walkthrough: SEIZE is both the English verb and French for sixteen, so 'a number of Parisians' means a number in French, not a group.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: to arrest is to take hold of someone, and French for sixteen is spelt the same.

clue.text: Widespread alarm about sea receding

indicators.note: a receding tide goes back, so the sea's letters run backwards
one thing placed about another surrounds it, so alarm wraps round the sea

parts.note: sudden alarm
the Med, the Mediterranean Sea, turned round

explanation.surface: People panic about the sea going out, as before a tsunami.
explanation.walkthrough: PAN(DEM)IC.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: as an adjective it means prevalent across a whole region or the world.

clue.text: British family in Fiji oddly lacking swimwear

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it, so the family goes inside what is left of Fiji

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for British

indicators.note: lacking its odd letters, so Fiji loses its first and third, leaving the even ones

parts.note: fIjI without F and J
your kin are your family

explanation.surface: A British family on holiday in Fiji has forgotten to pack costumes.
explanation.walkthrough: B + I(KIN)I.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a two-piece swimsuit.

clue.text: Did the same crossword as previously decided

definitions.text: Did the same crossword as previously
definitions.meaning: worked out the same puzzle a second time: RE- plus the past tense of solve

explanation.surface: Someone did last week's crossword a second time, having planned to.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as RE-SOLVED for the playful half.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: re-solved is worked out again, and as one word it means having made a firm decision.

clue.text: PA finally ready before the deadline

indicators.note: at the end, so take only the last letter of ready

parts.note: the last letter of readY
done ahead of time

explanation.surface: A personal assistant finally has the work ready ahead of the deadline.
explanation.walkthrough: PA looks like a personal assistant; it is per annum, Latin for each year.
explanation.definitionFit: An abbreviation: p.a., per annum, is Latin for each year.
